## Headline

Logitech International grew revenue to USD 1,218.8m [F:cur.revenue] in Q2 FY2027, up 2.8% [F:cur.revenue_yoy], the slowest year-on-year growth since Q4 FY2025. Margins held up: gross margin was 44.9% [F:cur.gross_margin] and operating margin 16.5% [F:cur.operating_margin], and net income rose 5.5% [F:cur.net_income_yoy] to USD 180.0m [F:cur.net_income]. Cash generation weakened, with free cash flow of USD 148.8m [F:cur.free_cash_flow] against USD 212.3m [F:ly.free_cash_flow] a year earlier.

## Growth and profitability

Revenue growth of 2.8% [F:q2_fy2027.revenue_yoy] compares with 6.9% [F:q1_fy2027.revenue_yoy] in Q1 FY2027 and 6.3% [F:ly.revenue_yoy] in Q2 FY2026. Only Q4 FY2025, at -0.1% [F:q4_fy2025.revenue_yoy], was weaker in the last eight quarters. For 6M FY2027, revenue reached USD 2,446.1m [F:ytd.revenue], up 4.8% [F:ytd.revenue_yoy]. The pack does not show why growth slowed.

Gross margin improved by +1.5 pp [F:cur.gross_margin_change_yoy] from 43.4% [F:ly.gross_margin] a year ago. It was well below the 49.5% [F:q1_fy2027.gross_margin] reported in Q1 FY2027, a figure flagged for checking below.

Operating expenses grew as a share of revenue. Selling and marketing rose to 18.0% [F:cur.selling_pct] of revenue from 16.8% [F:ly.selling_pct]. R&D rose to 6.8% [F:cur.rnd_pct] from 6.4% [F:ly.rnd_pct]. General and admin was flat at 3.5% [F:cur.admin_pct]. Higher spending absorbed most of the gross margin gain, so operating margin rose by only +0.3 pp [F:cur.operating_margin_change_yoy] from 16.1% [F:ly.operating_margin]. That is below the 21.1% [F:q1_fy2027.operating_margin] of Q1 FY2027 and the 20.1% [F:q3_fy2026.operating_margin] of Q3 FY2026.

Net margin was 14.8% [F:cur.net_margin], against 14.4% [F:ly.net_margin] a year earlier. For 6M FY2027, net income was USD 415.7m [F:ytd.net_income], up 31.3% [F:ytd.net_income_yoy]. Much of that strength came from the first quarter.

## Working capital and cash

Operating cash flow fell to USD 163.6m [F:cur.operating_cash_flow] from USD 228.8m [F:ly.operating_cash_flow]. Trailing-twelve-month cash conversion eased to 1.25x [F:cur.cash_conversion_ttm] from 1.29x [F:ly.cash_conversion_ttm], which is still comfortably above net income.

Inventory rose 7.6% [F:cur.inventory_yoy] to USD 556.8m [F:cur.inventory], growing faster than revenue. A year earlier, inventory had fallen 0.5% [F:ly.inventory_yoy]. Days inventory outstanding reached 75 days [F:q2_fy2027.dio_days], the highest of the last eight quarters, up from 66 days [F:q1_fy2027.dio_days] in Q1 FY2027 and 70 days [F:ly.dio_days] a year ago.

Days payables outstanding lengthened to 87 days [F:cur.dpo_days] from 79 days [F:ly.dpo_days]. This more than offset the inventory build, so the cash conversion cycle shortened to 44 days [F:cur.cash_conversion_cycle_days] from 46 days [F:ly.cash_conversion_cycle_days]. Days sales outstanding were unchanged at 55 days [F:cur.dso_days].

Share buybacks of USD 170.8m [F:cur.buybacks] exceeded free cash flow in the quarter and were well above the USD 106.6m [F:ly.buybacks] of Q2 FY2026. Cash and cash equivalents stood at USD 1,507.6m [F:cur.cash], up from USD 1,375.8m [F:ly.cash] a year earlier.

- **Revenue momentum:** whether growth recovers from 2.8% [F:cur.revenue_yoy] or slows further. The pack does not explain the slowdown.

- **Supplier terms:** the cash conversion cycle now relies on longer payables of 87 days [F:cur.dpo_days], which may not last.
- **Operating spending:** whether selling and marketing at 18.0% [F:cur.selling_pct] of revenue keeps eroding the gross margin gains.
- **Capital returns:** whether buybacks continue to exceed free cash flow.
- **Q1 FY2027 margins:** whether the first-quarter figures are confirmed or revised.
